publication_date_basis: GitHub commit time of the author's commit 56c59854 in Majdoddin/formal-math (the repository push was 2026-11-20T17:58:14Z). Version 2 of arXiv:2610.17420; it is not yet on arXiv. The author proposed this randomized claim in bigospeedrun/site issue 26.
theorem: Corollary 23.5 of version 2 (split random covering), via Theorem 23.3 and the certified points of Table 11
model_check: Corollary 23.5: APSP on directed n-vertex graphs with integer weights of absolute value n^O(1) and no negative cycles has a Monte Carlo algorithm with error probability n^(-C), for every constant C, in worst-case time O(n^2.98989). The proof computes the exponent 2.9898857... and absorbs the polylogarithmic factors by rounding up in the fifth decimal, so O(n^2.98989) is the stated bound. The problem is the one of the deterministic board (directed, polynomially bounded integer weights, no negative cycles, all ordered pairs). The paper does not define a randomized word RAM: it draws uniform random masks and a uniformly random prime and counts steps of a word RAM with O(log N)-bit words. Reading each random word as one step is our interpretation, as in the Monte Carlo statement proposed in issue 26. Source comparison, not a proof check.

verification: Written proof, not peer reviewed. The certified points behind the exponent (Table 11, Theorem 23.3) are exact-rational scripts r155_fold.py, r224_unfold_check.py and r154c_cert.py in the repository (scripts/ at that commit). The paper says the margins are small and that none of this is machine-checked. No Big O Speedrun proof check. Evidence remains Claimed.
